branches.source_phrase_ar: اللدة نقصانه الواو لأن أصله ولدة (maqayis)؛ لدة الرجل تربه؛ وهما لدان والجمع لدات ولدون (sihah)؛ اللدة مختصة بالترب يقال فلان لدة فلان وتربه (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği aynı yaşta olan denk kişidir; tekil, ikili ve çoğul biçim bilgileri bu yaştaşlık ilişkisini sayı bakımından çeşitlendirir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه اللدة أو لدة الرجل بمعنى تربه ومثيله في السن.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل هنا الولد بمعنى الابن ولا الوالد ولا التولد.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnız kanıtta verilen sabit söyleyişin anlamını karşılar; yalın bir sözcük anlamı olarak kullanılamaz.

error_profile.preserves: Durumun büyüklük ve ağırlık yönüyle şeyin bolluk yönünü birlikte korur.

concept_gloss.text: çok büyük bir durum ya da pek bol bir şey

concept_map.definition: Yalnız belirli bir kalıp söz içinde, çok büyük veya ağır bir durumu ya da çok bol bir şeyi anlatır. Söyleyişin kökeni baskına bağlanır; çok yiyecek ve çok otlak bolluk örnekleridir.

facets.statement: Kalıp söz çok büyük, önemli veya ağır bir durumu anlatır.
Aynı kalıp söz çok bol bir şeyi anlatmak için de kullanılır.
Söyleyişin çıkışı, baskın sırasında yaşanan ağır duruma bağlanır.
Çok yiyecek ve çok otlak, bolluk yönünün açık örnekleridir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kalıp söz büyük, önemli ve ağır bir olay veya durum için söylendiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Durumun olağanüstü büyüklük ve ağırlık derecesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kalıp söz yiyecek veya otlak gibi bir şeyin çokluğunu anlatırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bir şeyin olağanüstü bolluk derecesini ilgili bağlamda korur.

error_profile.adds: Gerçek bir çocuğun çağrılmadığı sıradan bir olayı anlamın içine ekler.
error_profile.collision: Sabit söyleyişin yerleşmiş anlamını sözcüğü sözcüğüne bir olayla karıştırır.
error_profile.loses: Çok büyük veya ağır durum ile çok bol şey bildiren yerleşmiş anlamı kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Kalıbın sözcük düzeyindeki çağırma ve çocuk görüntüsünü korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız verilen kalıp sözde geçerlidir; tek başına çocuk adını veya bu kalıp dışında kalan her büyüklük ve bolluk durumunu kapsamaz.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yalnız sabit bir söyleyiş içinde çok büyük veya ağır bir durumu ve çok bol bir şeyi anlatır; kökeni baskına bağlar, yiyecek ve otlağı bolluk örnekleri olarak verir. Ön çerçevedeki süt örneği yetkili kaynak ifadesinde bulunmadığından tanım bu örneği dışarıda bırakacak biçimde yeniden kurulmalıdır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: çok büyük veya ağır bir durum yahut çok bol bir şey için söylenen kalıp söz

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız verilen sabit söyleyişe bağlıdır; buradaki büyüklük, ağırlık ve bolluk anlamları yalın kök anlamına genellenmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Verilen bütün komşu adayları değerlendirildi; hiçbiri bu sabit söyleyişin büyük olay ve bolluk sınırını doğrudan paylaşmadığından yayımlanacak yararlı bir karşılaştırma bulunmadı.
branches.source_phrase_ar: أمر لا ينادى وليده؛ قيل ذلك لكل أمر عظيم ولكل شيء كثير (sihah)؛ هو أمر لا ينادى وليده؛ أمر جليل شديد؛ أصله في الغارة؛ طعام لا ينادى وليده؛ عشب لا ينادى وليده (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, sabit söyleyişi büyük veya ağır durum ile bolluk arasında açıklar; çıkışını baskına bağlar ve yiyecek ile otlağı bolluk örnekleri olarak verir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه المثل لا ينادى وليده وما فسرته المصادر من أمر عظيم أو شديد، أو شيء كثير، أو غارة تذهل الأم عن ولدها، أو طعام ولبن وعشب كثير لا يحتاج فيه إلى نداء الوليد.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل هنا معنى الوليد المفرد خارج هذا التركيب، ولا كل شدة أو كثرة بلا هذا المثل.

root_profile.summary: Kökün ana alanı doğum çevresinde çocuk, öz ana baba, doğurma olayı ve yeni doğmuş çocuk adlandırmalarını kurar. Bundan nedene bağlı türeme, sonradan oluşturulma, aynı yaşta olma ve büyüklük ya da bolluk bildiren sabit bir söyleyiş gibi yerleşmiş yan dallar gelişir.

text.arabic_uthmani: وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ حُسْنًۭا ۖ وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ لِتُشْرِكَ بِى مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌۭ فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَآ ۚ إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ

baseline.text: İnsana anne babasına iyi davranmasını emrettik. Eğer onlar, hakkında bilgin olmayan bir şeyi bana ortak koşman için seni zorlarlarsa onlara itaat etme. Dönüşünüz banadır; yaptıklarınızı size bildireceğim.

findings.text: Anne babaya iyilik ile bilgisiz ortak koşmaya itaat etmeme aynı bağlı görev içinde tutulur; aile bağı güçlüdür ama Allah'a ortaklık taşıyan bir geçit değildir.
Anne babanın zorlaması, bilgiyi itaatle değiştirmeye çalışan bir baskı mekanizması olarak teşhis edilir.
Son dönüş ve bildirim, aile baskısının son hüküm yetkisini elinden alır; reddediş keyfî değil, herkesin yaptığı işin daha tam açığa çıkacağı hesaba bağlıdır.

activation_trace.role: A connected trust passed onward makes filial care a durable charge rather than a passing preference.
The two parents as sources of birth locate the real relational claim that the charge protects.
Beneficent, well-made action defines what remains due in conduct.
Pressing another to the limit supplies the coercive force that tests the relation.
Introducing another into a shared claim identifies the demanded participation as an illegitimate co-claim.
Compliance is the specifically blocked channel, leaving beneficence itself unrevoked.

changed_reading.after: The ayah distinguishes an enduring relation of beneficence from a command-specific obedience channel that closes when kinship is used to recruit association.
changed_reading.before: Goodness to parents appears to imply broad filial compliance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَصَّيْنَا ... بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا is retained on one side of وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ ... فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا.
baseline_models.mechanism: The connected charge establishes durable beneficence toward the two sources of one's birth, but their effort can press that bond into an unauthorized partnership. The prohibition severs compliance with that command without severing the prior obligation of good conduct.

activation_trace.role: Categorical negation removes any present warrant from the proposed object of association.
A distinguishing mark that reveals and guides supplies the missing evidentiary criterion.
Return to the point of origin relocates final adjudication beyond the family command.
The arriving, consequential report makes divine disclosure the answer to unsupported assertion.
Purposive deeds, not inherited claims alone, become the object of the final report.

changed_reading.after: The ayah stages a provenance audit: kinship cannot supply the missing mark of truth, and contested authority is resolved by return and disclosure of each purposive response.
changed_reading.before: The child should refuse because the parents propose something unknown.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ is answered by إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The demanded partner has no disclosed mark by which the claim can be recognized, so inherited authority cannot manufacture warrant. Return brings all parties back to the source of judgment, where a consequential report discloses their intentional deeds.

activation_trace.role: Exhaustion through mixing or repeated use supplies a process image for pressure wearing down resistance.
The hunter's snare turns association into a capture mechanism rather than only a proposition.
Mutual accommodation names the relational concession by which pressure could become compliance.
The self's making an act easy marks the internalized endpoint that the prohibition blocks.

changed_reading.after: The ayah can also diagnose a gradual capture process in which intimacy, repetition, and accommodation make unsupported association feel voluntarily easy.
changed_reading.before: The parents issue a direct doctrinal command that must be rejected.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: جَٰهَدَاكَ لِتُشْرِكَ ... فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا anchors a process in which pressure seeks eventual willing accommodation.
baseline_models.mechanism: Parental striving can operate less as one explicit order than as repeated relational mixing that exhausts resistance. The partnership demand then functions like a snare, while mutual accommodation and the self's easing of an act describe the capture point that the refusal interrupts.

activation_trace.role: Pressure that carries the child to hardship is the focus-level force under examination.
Testing a person as metal is tested turns declared belief into something whose composition must be exposed.
The repeated assay establishes testing as the opening process rather than an incidental hardship.
Exerting full capacity under difficulty supplies a Godward effort whose benefit loops back to the agent.
The self as the very identity of the person fixes the beneficiary and owner of the striving.
Divine independence removes any inference that God needs the child's resistance.

changed_reading.after: It is a concentrated assay of professed belief: coercive effort reveals whether the child directs self-owned agency toward an unsupported partner or toward God without imagining that God needs the act.
changed_reading.before: The ayah is a local exception within filial ethics.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening context places professed belief in an assay, then makes striving reflexive: its yield returns to the striver's own self while God remains independent. Against that frame, the parents' striving is not evidence of a divine need or a superior claim; it is the local force through which the child's direction of agency is tested.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies assay, repeated striving, self-benefit, and divine independence; I assign the directional contrast between self-owned Godward effort and parental effort aimed at association. A live alternative is that the repeated root gives only a broad perseverance theme.
structural_cues: 29:2-3 place claims of belief under testing before the filial case.
29:6 repeats جهد reflexively and names the self as beneficiary while declaring God independent.

activation_trace.role: Common return brings every participant back for judgment without merging their agency.
The final report targets each party's purposive doing rather than the command's family provenance.
Purposive deeds are evaluated and rewarded, establishing action as the operative unit of account.
The best recompense for enacted good sharpens the distinction between conduct and mere affiliation.
Following in another's wake supplies the same delegated-agency structure that filial obedience could enact.
Bearing moral trust or burden frames the false promise that another can take over liability.
Sin as culpable error identifies what the would-be guides promise, but fail, to carry.
Weight that remains weight makes the leaders' added burdens cumulative rather than substitutive.

changed_reading.after: Refusal also blocks a false delegation of moral agency: neither affection nor obedience lets the originators of the command carry away the child's liability for acting on it.
changed_reading.before: Refusal protects the child from accepting a false proposition.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby invitation to follow another path is coupled to an offer to carry the follower's sins; the offer is denied, while misleaders acquire additional burdens without unloading those they misled. The focus return and report therefore make filial obedience morally nontransferable: parents can pressure or mislead, but they cannot absorb the child's enacted association.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a structurally parallel command to follow and an explicit failed liability transfer; I map that speech-act pattern onto the parents' demand. The alternative is that 29:12 concerns public ideological leaders only, though the agency rule still bears on the focus.
structural_cues: 29:12 says, in effect, follow our path and we will carry your sins, then immediately denies the transfer.
29:13 assigns misleaders their own loads plus added loads, not the removal of the followers' loads.

activation_trace.role: Joining one thing to another preserves a real ethical connection even when obedience is interrupted.
Beneficence keeps the surviving relation positively defined rather than merely tolerated.
A shared claim marks the point where relational connection becomes impermissible participation.
Love and affection supply the social adhesive by which false objects bind a group.
The connection standing between parties makes that affection an actual social structure.
Movement from one abode to another provides a non-hostile directional break toward the Lord.

changed_reading.after: Kindness preserves affection while refusal prevents affection itself from becoming the glue of association; even separation can be directional fidelity rather than repudiation of kin.
changed_reading.before: Kindness and doctrinal refusal are adjacent but independent duties.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later, objects taken besides God become a bond of worldly affection between people, but that bond reverses into mutual repudiation; Abraham then moves from one abode toward his Lord. This sharpens the focus distinction: filial affection and beneficence remain real goods, yet they must not become the connective material that stabilizes association, and directional separation need not mean hatred of kin.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies affection as social glue, its eschatological reversal, migration, and renewed descendants; I infer that the focus regulates family affection before it hardens into cultic solidarity. The live alternative is that 29:25 describes civic idol-bonds rather than kinship specifically.
structural_cues: 29:25 makes worldly affection around false objects end in mutual rejection and cursing at resurrection.
29:26 turns immediately to Abraham's migration toward his Lord, while 29:27 restores descendants and inherited gifts rather than erasing lineage.

activation_trace.role: Parents as the sources of birth supply the focus's closest natural protective authority.
Assigning a partner to God identifies the point at which protection is promoted into rival authority.
Actual disclosure to the knower, rather than social confidence, is the required warrant.
Making a thing appear good explains how misdirected deeds can feel evidentially persuasive.
Purposive deeds are the material that appearance beautifies and redirects.
Turning away and diverting converts persuasive appearance into path-blocking force.
Heart-insight remaining compatible with misdirection warns that felt discernment is not sufficient proof.
Taking charge of an affair supplies the protective office wrongly installed besides God.
Shelter and dwelling materialize the promise of safety made by such an authority.
Loss of strength exposes the protective structure's failure under load.
True knowing is what would disclose the weakness hidden by the shelter image.

changed_reading.after: The ayah also refuses to treat legitimate closeness and protection as self-authenticating evidence: a household authority becomes structurally weak when made a partner-authority beside God.
changed_reading.before: Parents can assert an unwarranted religious proposition despite their legitimate status.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah shows decorated deeds blocking a path even while their agents possess apparent insight, then pictures protectors besides God as a shelter whose structure is weakest. The focus's lack of knowledge therefore reaches beyond missing information: the felt security of a parent, household, or guardian cannot serve as proof when that protective office is converted into associational authority.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies misleading appearance, apparent insight, protective office, shelter, weakness, and knowledge; I infer a household-authority analogy because the focus names parents. The analogy is not an identification of parents with the spider house and should remain qualified.
structural_cues: 29:38 joins beautified deeds, obstruction of the path, and agents described as discerning.
29:41 joins protectors besides God, a house, structural weakness, and the counterfactual of knowledge.

activation_trace.role: Beneficent action supplies the continuing manner of response.
Coercive pressure that carries another to hardship defines the manner not to reciprocate.
The bounded refusal targets submission to the demand rather than every form of relation.
Doing what is best gives the refusal a constructive interpersonal mode.
Divine oneness without partner states the nonnegotiable content protected by the boundary.
Handing over and yielding fixes submission on God rather than on the coercive human command.
Full exertion under difficulty reverses the direction of striving from recruitment into association to fidelity in God.
Gentle indication toward the true path contrasts guidance with the parents' coercive pressure.
The doers of beneficence close the surah by reconnecting resistance to حسن.

changed_reading.after: Do not obey is a positive discipline: resist the coercive vector, keep the best mode of conduct, yield only to the One, and let difficult striving be answered by guidance rather than counter-pressure.
changed_reading.before: Do not obey is primarily a negative exception to a positive filial rule.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later instruction preserves the best mode while affirming one God and yielding to Him, and the closing reprise gives striving a different direction: effort in God is met by gentle guidance into paths and culminates in the doers of good. The focus refusal is thus disciplined noncompliance, not reciprocal coercion: it withholds submission from the parents' aim while continuing حسن.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated حسن, one God, surrender, striving, gentle guidance, and the closing muhsinin; I infer a sustained ethic of kind noncompliance. The alternative is that 29:46 governs a different interlocutor class, but 29:69 still reconnects the focus roots directly.
structural_cues: 29:46 coordinates the best manner, divine oneness, and surrender to God.
29:69 answers striving with guidance into multiple paths and closes on المحسنين.

activation_trace.role: Connection between things lets the ethical bond persist without requiring shared location or direction.
The birth relation remains the bond carried through any relocation.
Return to the ultimate point of origin provides the focus's larger destination.
Departure from one abode to another toward the Lord supplies a faithful spatial separation.
Expansive space contrary to constriction makes coercive locality nonfinal.
Each self as the person in identity individualizes the journey and its accountability.
Universal return repeats the focus destination after the command to inhabit God's wide earth.

changed_reading.after: Return also supplies a larger home from which present coercive locality can be left: distance may interrupt obedience or residence without cancelling filial beneficence.
changed_reading.before: To Me is your return functions mainly as a future warning after the family dispute.

context_deltas.mechanism: Migration toward the Lord, the widening of God's earth, and every self's return make the focus's return clause a larger spatial and temporal home. Filial goodness can remain connected across distance, while obedience and residence are allowed to separate when the local household becomes coercive.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies migration, spatial width, individual selfhood, and return; I infer that these make the filial obligation portable when pressure requires distance. The alternative is that the migration frame concerns public persecution rather than a household conflict.
structural_cues: 29:26 names movement toward the Lord after a social rupture.
29:56-57 place wide earth, individual mortality, and return to God in immediate sequence.

remaining_uncertainties: The household, spider-house, and shore correspondences are reader-supplied analogies rather than explicit identifications.
The marker branch of ع ل م sharpens the epistemic model, but ordinary knowledge may carry most of the clause's force.
The ط و ع to س ط ع house-pole activation is licensed by the packet's split mapping but remains deliberately form-distant.
strongest_changes: The opening assay and reflexive striving turn the family conflict into a test of self-owned direction rather than a contest between divine and parental needs.
The follow-and-carry-burdens sequence makes obedience nontransferable moral agency: parents may mislead but cannot remove the child's liability.
Affection, household protection, migration, and wide earth distinguish preserving kinship from installing kinship as rival authority.
The closing pairing of striving, gentle guidance, and muhsinin recovers حسن as the manner of resistance, making the command disciplined kind noncompliance.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly separated closeness, affection, shelter, and guidance from coercive following. It changed a filial exception into a portable ethics of beneficence with bounded obedience, evidentiary discipline, and nontransferable accountability.

activation_trace.role: An erected tent-pole gives withheld compliance the material role of support not supplied to a false structure.
Association identifies the structure whose rival claim must not be propped up.
Shelter and dwelling provide the context structure that would require support.
Weakness under load explains why the associational shelter cannot truly stand.

changed_reading.after: Materially, the refusal can be pictured as withholding the supporting pole by which a sheltering but associational household claim would appear able to stand.
changed_reading.before: The child simply declines to comply with the parents' command.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant ط و ع to س ط ع mapping and a material house analogy, not the ordinary sense of obedience. It remains anchored in فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا and is cross-checked by the weak-house image in 29:41; downstream prose should present it only as a form-distant structural analogy, never as the lexical meaning of the clause.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The split mapping for تُطِعْ supplies an erected house-pole image at the exact point where compliance is withheld.

activation_trace.role: Parents as sources of birth supply the ordinary relation of origin and safety in the analogy.
Association with God names the compromise demanded within that safe relation.
Exclusive separation from association supplies the clarity produced under danger.
Obedient yielding locates crisis devotion wholly with God.
Dry land supplies the restored zone of ordinary safety where exclusive orientation is tested again.
Renewed association after rescue supplies the reversal that the focus boundary guards against.

changed_reading.after: It may also be read as a shore test: the return to familiar relational safety is precisely where crisis-clear exclusivity can soften back into association.
changed_reading.before: Parental pressure is an isolated doctrinal conflict inside the family.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the focus never calls parents a shore and 29:65 describes a broader crisis-to-safety reversal. It remains anchored in the focus's parents, obedience, and association and in the context's explicit movement from exclusive devotion at sea to renewed association on land; render it as an analogy about ordinary safety reactivating compromise, not as an identification of family with unbelief.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The parents are the ayah's nearest relation of origin and safety, yet their pressure aims at تُشْرِكَ and tests whether exclusive orientation survives ordinary closeness.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A joined charge with a guarded joint.** و ص ي B001 is “joining one thing to another,” and B002 is “a charge joined to another person.” Goodness to parents and refusal of their unsupported demand are placed in one construction rather than offered as alternatives. I infer that the charge joins duties without collapsing their boundaries; filial goodness reads as a durable bond whose joint must not transmit association with God.
2. **Coercive effort exposed by its object.** ج ه د B003 is pressing someone to strain. The parents' effort is grammatically aimed at لِتُشْرِكَ and lacks علم, so pressure serves as a causal mechanism attempting to replace knowledge with obedience. The ayah therefore reads as diagnosing coerced allegiance, not as licensing generalized disobedience.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Abraham's migration in 29:26 supplies a surprising consequence of guarded refusal: maintaining the knowledge-boundary may require spatial separation without dissolving the original obligation to goodness.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A joined family charge has an epistemic boundary.** Lexical evidence: `وَصَّيْنَا`, root `و ص ي`, `B002` (a charge joined to another person); `وَالِدَيْهِ`, root `و ل د`, `B002` (parents by birth relation); `لِتُشْرِكَ`, root `ش ر ك`, `B001` (sharing and partnership); and `عِلْم`, root `ع ل م`, `B001` (knowing as clear). Structural cue: the syntax first joins goodness to parents, then blocks pliant obedience (`ط و ع B001`) exactly where they press for an unsupported partnership. Assigned role: the charge binds the child to parents; knowledge limits what may be bound to God. Abductive move: the packet supplies both bond and prohibition; I infer that relational goodness does not authorize an epistemically groundless transfer of ultimate allegiance. Reading change: filial duty is strong but internally bounded, not an undifferentiated command to comply.

2. **Pressure is answered by return and disclosure, not counter-coercion.** Lexical evidence: `جَاهَدَاكَ`, root `ج ه د`, `B003` (pressing someone to strain); `مَرْجِعُكُمْ`, root `ر ج ع`, `B001` (return); and `فَأُنَبِّئُكُم`, root `ن ب ء`, `B002` (news brought and reported). Structural cue: `29:6` defines beneficial striving as self-returning, while `29:10-13` expose social pressure, hidden allegiance, and failed burden transfer before final questioning. Assigned role: ultimate return relocates adjudication away from the coercive family encounter; disclosure makes actual work reportable. Abductive move: I infer that the promised report neutralizes the pressure's claim to final authority. Reading change: refusal remains accountable and non-arbitrary because all parties return to a fuller disclosure of what they did.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: - **Later correction (`29:46-47`):** Shared revelation and best-form dialogue show that bounded obedience need not become relational contempt or indiscriminate severance. The family charge in `29:8` is retrospectively one instance of a broader rule: preserve goodness and common truth while refusing unsupported partnership.

words.gloss_range: opening connective that both resumes a new legal unit and links it to the prior reward-accounting movement
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as a connected launch: the filial command is new, yet still tied to the prior reward-accounting movement (29:7). Its fusion to {{ar:وَصَّيْنَا}} ({{tr:waṣṣaynā}}) also gives the opening a repeated w-onset, so the transition into divine enjoinment feels joined rather than abrupt. The local verbal frame rules out an oath reading.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following divine enjoinment verb to which the opening connective is fused

topics.headline: connected discourse launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the parental command is not isolated; it enters as a new legal unit still joined to the prior moral-accounting frame.
topics.reason: The opening connective can resume and coordinate, and the following divine verb anchors a new but linked clause.

topics.blocking_evidence: The following finite divine verb and boundary discourse do not license an oath opening.
topics.headline: oath opening blocked
topics.reason: The following finite verb and discourse boundary select resumption or coordination, not an oath frame.

words.gloss_range: completed divine enjoinment concerning parents; directive, weighty, and not mere advice
words.prose: {{ar:وَصَّيْنَا}} ({{tr:waṣṣaynā}}) makes the parental duty a completed divine charge, not inherited custom or negotiable advice. Its Form II pressure and embedded divine subject make the command weighty, while the wider parental formula also echoes 31:14 and 46:15 with this ayah's sharper move toward the shirk exception.
words.root_gloss_range: binding instruction, charge, testamentary direction, and connection; here selected as divine enjoinment

topics.headline: completed divine enjoinment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees filial duty sourced in a completed divine speech-act, not in parental authority alone.
topics.reason: The perfect Form II verb with first-person plural subject supports a directive divine charge.

topics.headline: durable binding instruction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command carries testament-like durability and joining force, while local syntax keeps enjoinment as the selected sense.
topics.reason: Testament and joining pressure survive as force around the directive sense, without replacing the local enjoinment reading.

topics.headline: parental charge formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a familiar parental-duty formula, specialized here by the immediate theological limit (31:14; 46:15).
topics.reason: The phrase recurs in parental-duty contexts and 29:8 compresses it toward the exception clause.

words.gloss_range: the generic human as direct recipient of the charge, universal yet grammatically singular and personally accountable
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ}} ({{tr:al-insāna}}) is a singular generic object: all humanity is addressed through one accountable human. That single form lets the universal command become personal before the ayah turns to the singular pressured addressee, and its social or forgetfulness derivation pressure fits a reminder about parents and divine limits.
words.root_gloss_range: human/social-perceptive field with contested forgetfulness pressure; here the generic human recipient is selected

topics.headline: generic human recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the charge falls on the human as a class while still landing on one accountable person.
topics.reason: The accusative definite singular is the direct object of the divine charge and functions generically.

topics.headline: singular universal made personal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees universal humanity compressed into one case, then localized in the intimate parent relation.
topics.reason: The singular generic form and following possessed dual parents create the universal-to-intimate movement.

topics.headline: sociality and reminder pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the human as socially bound and in need of reminder, while the local noun remains the generic human.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is useful pressure, but it does not replace the local generic-human sense.

words.gloss_range: governed preposition marking the parents as the domain or concern of the charge, not its instrument
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) makes the parent phrase the governed concern of the divine charge. The preposition prevents the parents from becoming the bare object of the verb: the command is concerning them, while goodness supplies the required conduct or quality.

topics.headline: parents as governed concern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the syntax charges the human concerning parents rather than making parents the direct object of the charging verb.
topics.reason: The waṣṣā-plus-preposition frame marks the parental domain of the charge.

topics.blocking_evidence: The prepositional phrase is governed by the divine charging verb as its topic, not as an instrument.
topics.headline: instrumental reading blocked
topics.reason: The local government selects concerning or specification; parents are not the means by which the charge is issued.

words.gloss_range: the human's own two begetting parents, possessed and dual, recipients of goodness and possible agents of pressure
words.prose: {{ar:وَٰلِدَيْهِ}} ({{tr:wālidayhi}}) names the human's own two begetting parents: dual, possessed, and governed by the charge. The same pair can receive commanded goodness and later become agents of pressure, so the word holds origin-based obligation together with a coming authority test.
words.root_gloss_range: birth, begetting, offspring, origin, and parenthood; here the active-participle parental-origin sense is selected

topics.headline: owned dual parent relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the universal human is immediately bound to each person's own two parents.
topics.reason: The dual genitive with possessive suffix anchors both parents as the charged relation.

topics.headline: begetting-origin pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the obligation grounded in origin and begetting, while local grammar keeps the word as the parent dual.
topics.reason: The active-participle and birth-field pressure sharpen why parents matter without turning the word into a broader biology claim.

topics.headline: recipients can become pressure agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same parents move from recipients of goodness to possible agents of theological pressure (31:14; 46:15).
topics.reason: The dual referent is preserved into the later dual verb and belongs to familiar parental-duty passages.

words.gloss_range: open-ended goodness toward parents, both quality of treatment and enjoined content, with canonical noun force
words.prose: {{ar:حُسْنًۭا}} ({{tr:ḥusnan}}) is the ethical payload of the opening command. Its accusative role can be heard as the quality of treatment and as the enjoined content, while the canonical noun keeps goodness broad and substantive. Variant pressure toward {{ar:إِحْسَانًا}} ({{tr:iḥsānan}}) makes active beneficence audible as a contrast, but the local wording lands first on the quality of goodness before obedience's theological limit.
words.root_gloss_range: beauty, moral goodness, excellence, and beneficence; here goodness as filial quality/content is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: variant pressure toward active beneficence, contrasted with the canonical noun of goodness

topics.headline: goodness as quality and content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that goodness is not a small manner note; it is both how the charge is enacted and what it commands.
topics.reason: The accusative allows manner/cognate/content pressure, all tied to the parental charge.

topics.headline: moral beauty of conduct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels filial conduct as morally beautiful, not merely procedurally correct.
topics.reason: The root field supports the ethical-aesthetic force of the local goodness noun.

topics.headline: canonical noun with variant pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the canonical noun stays broad while variants and formulae press toward active beneficence (31:14; 46:15).
topics.reason: Variant pressure clarifies quality versus action, but the local canonical form remains the noun of goodness.

words.gloss_range: hinge connective introducing the conditional exception while keeping it tied to the filial command
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the internal hinge. It keeps the exception coordinated with the filial baseline while pivoting sharply into the condition that limits obedience.

topics.headline: hinge from duty to exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the theological exception grows out of the filial command instead of cancelling or detaching from it.
topics.reason: The conjunction before the conditional both links and pivots from baseline duty to boundary case.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle presenting parental pressure as possible and legally framed rather than assumed as normal
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) frames the conflict as a condition, not the normal definition of parents. The perfect verb inside the condition lets a fully realized pressure-event be handled as a legal possibility, then answered by a prohibition.

topics.headline: possible condition not assumed norm
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that parental pressure toward shirk is treated as a possible exception, preserving the baseline command of goodness.
topics.reason: The conditional particle makes the event contingent rather than expected.

topics.headline: complete legal condition-response span
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the middle of the ayah as a rule-governed condition and answer, not a loose story.
topics.reason: The conditional spans the pressure clause and the apodosis through the refusal command.

words.gloss_range: directed exertion by both parents against one singular addressee, narrowed here to coercive religious pressure
words.prose: {{ar:جَٰهَدَاكَ}} ({{tr:jāhadāka}}) compresses both parents acting against one addressee into one verb. The root's effort force survives, but the purpose clause narrows it away from battlefield struggle into directed pressure toward shirk, with the same exception pattern visible in 31:15 and a contrast to self-striving in 29:6.
words.root_gloss_range: strenuous effort, exertion, contending, and struggle; here Form III pressure toward a theological goal is selected

topics.headline: dual pressure on singular you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the social pressure grammatically: two parents press one addressed human.
topics.reason: The dual subject marker and singular object suffix encode the pressure relation.

topics.headline: striving redirected toward shirk
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that effort itself is not validated; its goal decides whether striving becomes coercive misdirection.
topics.reason: The purpose clause selects religious coercion, not martial combat, while preserving strenuous exertion.

topics.headline: exception formula and direct address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a known parental-pressure formula (31:15) and a local contrast with self-striving (29:6).
topics.reason: The same cluster and nearby root recurrence frame the family conflict as a test of directed effort.

words.gloss_range: purposive/result lām that makes the parents' pressure goal explicit: association with God
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) ties the parents' striving to a specific theological aim. Whether heard as intended purpose or resulting outcome, the particle makes obedience unsafe because the pressure terminates in association with God.

topics.headline: pressure has a named goal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the conflict is defined by its theological aim, not by parental insistence in general.
topics.reason: The lām phrase attaches to the striving verb and governs the following subjunctive.

topics.headline: purpose or result still dangerous
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that even a result reading keeps the boundary intact: compliance would lead into the prohibited association.
topics.reason: The local clause licenses purpose most directly, while result nuance still supports the same refusal.

words.gloss_range: unrealized purpose verb for actively assigning a partner with God; the object is left open then narrowed by no-knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:تُشْرِكَ}} ({{tr:tushrika}}) is not a completed act but the purpose toward which pressure is directed. Its Form IV makes the human an active assigner of partnership, and the following open object plus no-knowledge clause defines the prohibited association by epistemic failure rather than by naming one idol.
words.root_gloss_range: sharing, partnership, association, and having a share; here unauthorized divine association is selected

topics.headline: unrealized purpose verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that shirk is the parents' aim in the condition, not something already conceded as actual.
topics.reason: The purposive lām governs the imperfect as a subjunctive purpose verb.

topics.headline: active assigning of partnership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees shirk as actively making a co-sharer with God, not as passive confusion.
topics.reason: The sh-r-k field and Form IV morphology support active unauthorized association.

topics.headline: open object narrowed by knowledge clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the associated thing is left open, then defined by lack of knowledge.
topics.reason: The verb is completed by the divine prepositional phrase and the relative object clause.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus first-person divine suffix marking God as the one with whom association would be made
words.prose: {{ar:بِى}} ({{tr:bī}}) makes the offense directly Godward: the preposition governs the first-person divine suffix as the one with whom association would be made. This personal divine reference also joins the later return-to-Me frame.

topics.headline: God as governed complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that shirk is framed as a direct violation of the divine relation, not an abstract doctrinal error.
topics.reason: The preposition plus first-person suffix attaches to the association verb.

topics.headline: Me bracket through conflict and return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the divine voice narrow from legislation to personal claim and final return.
topics.reason: The first-person forms in the middle and closure bracket the theological core.

words.gloss_range: open relative object of association, narrowed by the following no-knowledge clause rather than named in advance
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens an unnamed object slot: whatever is being associated with God is identified only by the following no-knowledge clause. A negative-particle reading is visible only as a rejected pressure; the local structure works as a relative clause.

topics.headline: unnamed object of association
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibited object is not pre-named; it is any candidate that fails the knowledge test.
topics.reason: The particle fills the object slot and is specified by the following relative clause.

topics.headline: openness narrowed epistemically
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees openness and limit together: the object is broad, but only as defined by absence of knowledge.
topics.reason: The relative clause narrows the open pronoun by the knowledge predicate.

topics.blocking_evidence: The following negation verb already carries the negative force, while the clause needs a relative object for the association verb.
topics.headline: negative parse weakened
topics.reason: The following negation verb already supplies negation, making a negative-particle parse structurally strained here.

words.gloss_range: kopulative negation denying the addressee's knowledge about the associated thing, not simply negating an action
words.prose: {{ar:لَيْسَ}} ({{tr:laysa}}) negates an epistemic predicate: it says there is no knowledge for the addressee about the associated thing, not simply that the thing does not exist. The clause delays the knowledge noun to the end, making absence of knowledge the decisive landing point.
words.root_gloss_range: defective/stative negation of being or existence; here it negates possession of knowledge

topics.headline: negated possession of knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the boundary is epistemic: what is denied is the human's knowledge, not merely an object's existence.
topics.reason: The negation verb governs a nominal knowledge predicate through the possessive phrase.

topics.headline: knowledge denial pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the local no-knowledge clause as part of a broader pattern stripping false claims of valid footing.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence evidence links negation, knowledge, and association.

words.gloss_range: possessive dative focused on what knowledge belongs to the pressured addressee
words.prose: {{ar:لَكَ}} ({{tr:laka}}) centers the pressured addressee's own epistemic possession: the issue is what you have by way of knowledge concerning it. The local construction selects possession, not benefit, so the parents' pressure cannot substitute for the child's own verified knowledge.

topics.headline: your knowledge possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that responsibility is individualized: the deciding criterion is what you have knowledge of.
topics.reason: The possessive dative continues the singular addressee and forms the no-knowledge idiom.

topics.blocking_evidence: The predicate is knowledge in a negated possession construction, not a benefit phrase.
topics.headline: benefit sense blocked
topics.reason: The knowledge noun and negation construction select possession or attribution, not benefit.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus pronoun returning to the open object and marking the topic about which knowledge is absent
words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) loops the relative clause back to the unnamed object: it is the thing about which knowledge is absent. The repeated b-preposition sound binds {{ar:بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ}} ({{tr:bi-wālidayhi}}), {{ar:بِى}} ({{tr:bī}}), {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}), and later {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}), while each occurrence keeps a different function: parental topic, association, specification, then disclosure content.

topics.headline: about-it knowledge link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the no-knowledge test is tightly attached to the very object proposed for association.
topics.reason: The pronoun returns to the open object and the preposition marks the topic of denied knowledge.

topics.headline: repeated form different functions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees formal cohesion without flattening the preposition into one meaning across the ayah.
topics.reason: The repeated preposition appears with different local functions: parental topic, association, specification, and disclosure content.

words.gloss_range: any verified knowledge relevant to the proposed association; its negated indefiniteness makes absence decisive
words.prose: {{ar:عِلْمٌۭ}} ({{tr:ʿilmun}}) is the decisive boundary term. Because it is indefinite under negation, the clause denies any relevant verified knowledge for the addressee; parental obedience stops where knowledge for the proposed association is absent.
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, knowledge, signs, marks, and established information; here verified knowledge is the obedience boundary

topics.headline: no relevant knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse does not require a partial doubt; it names absence of any relevant knowledge.
topics.reason: The indefinite noun under negation gives the absence broad scope.

topics.headline: epistemology governs obedience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ethical rule grounded in verified knowledge, not preference or family pressure.
topics.reason: The knowledge root and recurring shirk/no-knowledge pattern make epistemic warrant the limit of compliance.

words.gloss_range: result particle marking the conditional answer and turning the scenario into a direct ruling
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the condition into its answer. The particle makes the refusal command follow as the legal consequence of parental pressure toward unsupported association.

topics.headline: then-answer of the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scenario is not left unresolved; it is immediately converted into a ruling.
topics.reason: The apodosis is prohibitive, so the result particle marks the conditional answer.

topics.headline: condition resolved into refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the logic: epistemic failure triggers non-obedience.
topics.reason: The particle carries result and causal force into the prohibition.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negator governing the obedience verb and limiting refusal to the specified case
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive, not merely descriptive negation. It governs the jussive obedience verb, so refusal becomes a commanded act within the specified shirk-pressure condition, not a general cancellation of filial goodness.

topics.headline: formal negative command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that non-obedience is actively commanded here, not merely reported as noncompliance.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following jussive verb as a prohibition.

topics.headline: scope limited to obedience verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the prohibition targets obedience in this case, not all goodness toward parents.
topics.reason: The compact apodosis confines the prohibition to the obedience verb under the condition.

words.gloss_range: active compliance with both parents, prohibited only in the shirk-pressure condition and distinguished from goodness
words.prose: {{ar:تُطِعْهُمَا}} ({{tr:tuṭiʿhumā}}) names the compliance that must be refused. Its dual suffix keeps both parents in view, but the root and Form IV make the issue active willing obedience, not the abandonment of goodness or care; 31:15 preserves the same exception logic.
words.root_gloss_range: willing compliance, obedience, yielding, and ability-related extensions; here active obedience is selected

topics.headline: do not obey both parents in this matter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both parents remain the object of the command, but only as compliance targets in the specified case.
topics.reason: The jussive prohibition and dual suffix bind the refusal to both parents under the condition.

topics.headline: compliance distinguished from goodness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that refusing obedience can coexist with moral treatment; compliance and goodness are not identical.
topics.reason: The root field supports active compliance, while the earlier goodness command remains in force.

topics.headline: parental exception formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the refusal as a specific parental-shirk exception formula, not a broad license for disobedience (31:15).
topics.reason: The cluster ties non-obedience to parental striving, shirk, and lack of knowledge.

words.gloss_range: fronted directional phrase making God the exclusive personal endpoint of return
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيَّ}} ({{tr:ilayya}}) front-loads the destination before the return noun: to Me is where the whole conflict ends. That fronting gives the closure exclusive force, placing parental authority under God as the final endpoint.

topics.headline: fronted return destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the authority question is answered by destination: return is to God, not to parents.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is fronted before the return noun and carries endpoint focus.

topics.headline: personal endpoint of return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the afterlife endpoint as personal and directional, not an abstract location.
topics.reason: The directional preposition plus first-person suffix contracts movement and divine endpoint.

words.gloss_range: the plural addressees' return to God, with place/time/event pressure and widened accountability
words.prose: {{ar:مَرْجِعُكُمْ}} ({{tr:marjiʿukum}}) widens the scene from one pressured child to a plural return. The mīm-noun can hold event, place, or time of return, and the root frames judgment as coming back to God, where parents and child alike are folded into final accountability. Echo-like return pressure makes choices and deeds come back for disclosure, while local syntax keeps the eschatological return as the selected sense.
words.root_gloss_range: returning, reverting, coming back, echoing, and restoration; here eschatological return is selected

topics.headline: singular trial widened to plural return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from singular pressure to plural accountability that includes all parties.
topics.reason: The suffix shifts from singular address to plural return.

topics.headline: return as event endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels judgment as return to source, while local syntax keeps the eschatological return as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The mīm-noun permits place/time/event pressure and the root gives return imagery without requiring speculative origin claims.

topics.headline: return then disclosure formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the filial conflict closed inside a wider return-to-God accounting motif (29:17).
topics.reason: The return root cooccurs with informing and deeds, and recurs in the surah's return motif.

words.gloss_range: sequencing particle that makes disclosure follow directly from the return clause
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) ties return directly to disclosure. The first result particle answered the condition; this second one turns arrival to God into immediate informing, giving the ayah two consequence beats: refusal now and audit later.

topics.headline: disclosure follows return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that return to God is not a bare endpoint; it immediately issues into disclosure.
topics.reason: The second result particle links the nominal return clause to the informing verb.

topics.headline: two consequence beats
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah as a chain of consequence: condition to refusal, return to disclosure.
topics.reason: The repeated particle marks consequence at two scales.

words.gloss_range: first-person divine informing of the plural addressees; detailed consequential disclosure after return
words.prose: {{ar:أُنَبِّئُكُمْ}} ({{tr:unabbiʾukum}}) shifts from the earlier divine plural to singular I, making the final accounting personally voiced. The Form II informing is consequential disclosure, not casual speech, and the doubled middle consonant makes that intensifying disclosure audible. Prophetic or elevation associations remain only background pressure around authoritative divine reporting.
words.root_gloss_range: significant news, report, informing, and authoritative disclosure; here Form II divine disclosure is selected

topics.headline: personal divine informing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the voice shift from majestic legislation to personal final disclosure.
topics.reason: The verb is first-person singular after the opening first-person plural divine charge.

topics.headline: detailed consequential informing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees final judgment as an explained disclosure of deeds, not a mute outcome.
topics.reason: The root and Form II morphology support significant, detailed informing.

topics.headline: authoritative report pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel authoritative disclosure from above, while the local verb remains God informing the addressees after return.
topics.reason: The n-b-ʾ/n-b-w dispute is useful as authority pressure but does not turn the scene into prophetic office language.

topics.headline: same plural audience in return and informing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the widened plural group remains the recipient of final disclosure.
topics.reason: The object suffix repeats the plural audience of the return noun.

words.gloss_range: content-marking preposition governed by the informing verb and pointing forward to the deeds clause
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the governed content marker of the informing verb. It points forward into the deeds clause, while also completing the ayah's thread of b-prepositions from parental duty through association and knowledge to final disclosure.

topics.headline: content governed by disclosure verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine informing is immediately given content, not left vague.
topics.reason: The informing verb selects the preposition to mark what the addressees will be informed about.

topics.headline: b-preposition thread to deeds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the repeated preposition thread gather duty, evidence, and disclosure into one closure.
topics.reason: The final preposition shifts from earlier functions to disclosure content.

words.gloss_range: open relative or gerundive content of final disclosure, covering what the addressees were doing
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the content to be disclosed: what they were doing, or their doing itself. Its openness reaches beyond the parent-shirk episode, and it reverses the earlier open object from hidden no-knowledge to exposed deed-record.

topics.headline: open object of final disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final audit covers the whole field of deeds, not only the immediate family-pressure incident.
topics.reason: The particle opens the disclosed content clause and remains broad before the habitual action phrase.

topics.headline: relative and gerundive both audit action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that either parse keeps habitual action as the audit content, while the local clause supplies the action phrase.
topics.reason: The surface alone permits both analyses; the following auxiliary-plus-verb clause licenses the audit reading.

topics.headline: unknown object becomes disclosed deeds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the particle pair: the first hides an unsupported object, the second opens the record to disclosure.
topics.reason: The repeated open pronoun links epistemic absence to final exposure.

words.gloss_range: auxiliary being with plural subject, forming past habitual action with the final verb
words.prose: {{ar:كُنتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) makes the final action habitual or ongoing in past time. The being verb turns deeds into a lived state, while the plural suffix keeps the same widened audience moving through return, disclosure, and audit.
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing, and state; here auxiliary past-state framing of action is selected

topics.headline: past habitual action frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the audit concerns sustained patterns of action, not only isolated acts.
topics.reason: The kāna-plus-imperfect construction forms a past habitual or ongoing action frame.

topics.headline: same plural group through closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the widened addressees built into the auxiliary before the final deed verb arrives.
topics.reason: The plural suffix continues the -kum/-tum chain.

topics.headline: doing as lived state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels deeds as part of what the addressees had been living, while local grammar keeps the verb auxiliary.
topics.reason: Being-state pressure survives through the auxiliary construction without importing place or creative-command senses.

topics.headline: formula prepares final deed word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the handoff from prior reward-accounting to direct second-person audit.
topics.reason: The k-w-n plus action-root formula recurs and here changes person into direct address.

words.gloss_range: purposeful deeds in a past-habitual frame, closing the ayah on accountable action
words.prose: {{ar:تَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:taʿmalūna}}) is the ayah's final landing: purposeful deeds under habitual disclosure. The Form I action root keeps the audit on the addressees' own morally accountable doing, and the boundary echo with 29:7 turns rewarded third-person deeds into second-person disclosure. Its final long plural ending leaves the ayah closing on ongoing shared action, not only on parents or shirk.
words.root_gloss_range: intentional doing, work, agency, and consequential action; here the addressees' own deeds are selected

topics.headline: sustained accountable doing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that judgment covers sustained morally accountable action, not accidental motion or one isolated deed.
topics.reason: The imperfect after the auxiliary gives habitual scope, and the action root selects purposeful doing.

topics.headline: own deeds not caused use
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the audit fall on the addressees' own deliberate deeds, while causative employment senses are not selected locally.
topics.reason: The local Form I verb selects basic purposeful action, not a causative putting-to-use construction.

topics.headline: 29:7 deed formula becomes direct audit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a recurring disclosure formula and sees the shift from what they did in 29:7 to what you were doing in 29:8.
topics.reason: The formula recurs broadly, and the local boundary changes person from reward report to direct audit.

topics.headline: final open plural cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes on ongoing plural action, not on parents or shirk alone.
topics.reason: Final position and plural imperfect cadence give deeds the closing weight.
